features.name: Cross-catalog model metadata fallback
features.description: Model refresh keeps every catalog source section instead of only the 13-provider price-sync allowlist, and when a provider's metadata lookup misses in its own catalog (metadataKey ?? providerKey) the worker falls back to a global by-model-id search across every catalog — trusted (price-sync allowlist) catalogs first, then the rest — so multi-vendor bundle providers (e.g. Qwen Token Plan serving deepseek-v4-pro / glm-5.2 ids from the qwen-keyed provider) resolve context window, token limits, modalities, and capability flags in the Console model library. Provider-scoped resolution keeps priority; each lookup form (raw id, vendor-stripped id, display name) is judged on its own — a form matching two or more trusted (tier-1) catalogs aborts the whole lookup, a form matching two or more untrusted (tier-2) catalogs is abandoned so the next form is tried, and a model that no form resolves in any catalog renders Unknown exactly as today. Prices are out of scope: registry entries carry no price fields, so the synced price columns remain the price_sync path's 13-provider responsibility and bundle-provider model prices stay empty. A cross-catalog hit records provenance in capability_metadata (resolvedVia: 'cross-catalog', resolvedFromCatalog: the source catalog key) for observability; provider-scoped and unresolved models omit these keys. Catalog source fetches share a per-URL in-memory cache (WORKER_MODEL_CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_MS, 0 disables) with single-flight and stale-on-error.

features.description: Grok's second routable face and its quota probe: the registry entry gains a responses endpoint from the same proxy base (the upstream's multi-agent grok variants are responses-only), the responses gateway filter extends its subscription allowlist from codex-only to codex-or-grok (with a guard that other subscription providers stay rejected), and the responses call path dispatches through the grok header adapter. quotaSource flips to supported with a new probe that issues GET /billing?format=credits and GET /billing against the proxy with the Bearer + X-XAI-Token-Auth headers, mapping the period usage percent (missing field treated as zero) to a windowed utilization with an RFC3339 resetsAt, and the legacy monthly config (USD-cent values where a zero serializes as an empty object, a non-positive monthly limit producing no window) to a monthly window; 401 maps to unauthorized, other failures to probe_failed, and a failed credits request degrades to the monthly window alone. Console shows both endpoint chips and the quota windows.
